intent.line: Intent: the product owner wants the reply/command scan to block recursive deletes on any variable or computed path, in the words of the ruling: "The reply/command scan must block rm -rf (and equivalents like Remove-Item -Recurse -Force) on any variable or computed path. Write the failing test first, reproducing tonight's exact slip." The reason given: a mis-quoted delete like the 2026-10-08 home-folder wipe could take out a repository including .git, losing every unpushed commit; so the same ruling puts one corrective card over the scan fix and push-on-every-commit. Why now: the open deletion-ban failure (F-071; audit 62) is a seat that ran rm -rf on a variable scratch path in card 226 criterion 1 while the reply scan, which reads only reply text, never saw the command. Stop the line; the scan is judged by the slip it failed to catch, so the first red reproduces that slip.
